lineage.prompt: A single monumental statue of a god carved from white marble with soft grey veining, in the manner of classical sculpture, standing in the relaxed contrapposto pose of Michelangelos David: weight on one leg, the other knee slightly bent, one arm hanging at the side, the other hand raised to the shoulder, head turned to the side with a stern gaze. The god has the likeness of the character in the reference image (a round, sturdy figure with a hawk nose and heavy brows, in a tailcoat with a torn sleeve and shin guards, a coiled serpent emblem on the chest), rendered entirely in stone: no colour, no paint, only pale marble. Carved in a slightly blocky, faceted, simplified way, like a chunky low-poly sculpture: broad planes, strong chisel facets, simplified hands and face, a strong readable silhouette. The whole statue visible from head to toe including its plain rough-hewn stone block seat or base, limbs clearly separated from the body. Plain flat mid-grey background, soft even studio light, no cast shadow on the background, no text, no other figures, no scenery.
